summary.headline: Neetu Yoshi reported FY26 total income of INR101 crore (up 44%) and PAT of INR25 crore (up 53%), with FY27 guidance of INR210-220 crore revenue at ~25% PAT margin.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 total income of about INR101 crore (up 44% YoY) and PAT of about INR25 crore (up 53% YoY), with positive cash flow. The new bogie plant (under 1 ton product capacity) was said to commence operations in June 2026, with first invoices expected in June and RDSO approval for the new plant expected around July. FY27 guidance is INR210-220 crore revenue with ~25% PAT margin, and H2 is expected to be higher than H1. Management described a INR29 crore warrant issue to fund working capital for the track section, which is expected to be deployed over 1.5-2 years.

financial_highlights.metric: Debtors as of 31 March (per analyst figure)
financial_highlights.change: about half collected by 15 April; ~INR20 crore pending per management

segments.name: Old plant (components, <100 kg products)
segments.commentary: Management targets about INR110 crore revenue from the existing plant in FY27. Wagon-related bogie prices reportedly fell from about INR3.25 lakh to INR2.70-2.80 lakh per unit.

segments.name: New bogie plant (<1 ton products)
segments.commentary: Expected to contribute about INR100 crore in FY27, with peak capacity of about INR200 crore. Products include bogies, couplers and crossings; capex of about INR77 crore, of which INR50 crore was spent (IPO funds per management).

segments.name: Track section
segments.commentary: Currently about INR20 crore revenue from sub-assembly; target INR60-70 crore within about two years. Requires rail procurement at INR65-70/kg versus scrap at INR37-39/kg, plus about 2 months inventory.

segments.name: Order book mix
segments.commentary: Roughly 20-30% track, about 40% coach, and the rest wagon-related (bogie and components). About 40% of sales are directly from government/Railways, rest private.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR210-220 crore with ~25% PAT margin; management said H2 will be higher than H1 as the new plant starts in June.
Peak revenue potential of about INR340-350 crore from both plants, expected next financial year (FY28), including track revenue of INR60-70 crore.
Management said it targets 25% PAT margin, and that the bottom line is the prime focus rather than revenue targets.
Exports targeted from next financial year (FY28), subject to precision engineering and quality capability (US/UK mentioned).
Wagon manufacturing facility targeted in about 3 years for 200 wagons.
Management expects receivable days to come down in FY27 to historical levels.
capex_capacity: New bogie plant ready; commencement expected within June 2026; RDSO approval for the new plant expected by next month (per management).
About INR10 crore of remaining bogie plant capex was reportedly utilised as of the call date; CWIP of about INR38 crore per analyst question, said to be substantially utilised post commissioning.
Next capex planned for complete assembly lines: casting, fabrication, spring and rubber plant; to be funded from internal accruals. No quantum disclosed.
Warrant proceeds (~INR29 crore) earmarked for track section working capital over 1.5-2 years.
Brownfield land available near the plant for further lines, per management.
demand_pricing: Railway payments are seasonal: funds run out in February-March and resume in April; about half of 31 March debtors were said to be collected by 15 April.
Raw material cost increases are passed through via Price Variation Clause (PVC) in railway tenders and a similar pass-through with private clients, with some lag by product.
Wagon industry saw a slowdown; management expects a new 1 lakh wagon order to revive demand.
Competitors named (unlisted): Frontera, Roys Steel, Atul Engineering. Management cites high entry barriers (RDSO/ICF/MCF/RCF approvals; 4-7 active clients per product).
Management says no slowdown in order flow; 15-20 products in RDSO/ICF/MCF/RCF approval pipeline, with timelines of 3-7 months per product.
Tax regime: 15% plus 2.5% cess (17.5%) under a central scheme for companies incorporated 2020-2024; no sunset clause per management, and benefit is exclusive of other incentives.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 revenue and PAT margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue INR210-220 crore and PAT margin of about 25%, with management expecting the same margin to carry forward.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise warrants if no funding needed for three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Track section requires working capital (rail at INR65-70/kg vs scrap INR37-39/kg, plus about 2 months inventory). Warrants of about INR29 crore to be used over 1.5-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book and execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: More than INR140-150 crore, executable within FY27. Mix: 20-30% track, ~40% coach, rest wagon-related.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 be higher than H1 in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, H2 is expected to be higher because the new plant starts in June, with 2-3 months already lost and linear growth thereafter.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a further capex plan and how is it funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Next capex is for complete assembly lines (casting, fabrication, springs, rubber) funded from internal accruals; no quantum given.

qa_highlights.question: Are exports planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets starting some exports from FY28, once precision and quality capability is in place (US/UK markets cited).

risks_watch: Receivables seasonality and collection timing: management said about INR20 crore of debtors was still pending as of the call; FY27 receivable days expected to fall.
RDSO/ICF/MCF/RCF approvals for new plant and 15-20 products pending; delays would push new revenue.
Ramp-up risk: new plant commencement slated for June, with first invoices expected in June; management said 2-3 months already lost.
Margin sustainability: management acknowledged margins erode as new entrants come in, and raw material cost increases pass through with lag.
Dilution via warrants (~INR29 crore) against a question on why debt was not used; management said no further dilution expected this year.
Concentration: about 40% of sales are direct from government, rest private; major revenue from Railways.
Inconsistencies in the call: revenue targets for FY28 ranged from INR340-350 crore to 350-400 crore; the call also cited a 1 lakh wagon order without confirmed timing.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, approvals and margins, but answers were often imprecise and inconsistent on numbers (e.g., plant capacity, FY28 revenue, debtors) and some questions went unanswered or were restated. Management was evasive on the rationale for equity-funded working capital versus debt.
key_quotes: So, the revenue guidance for this current financial year what we have given is around INR210 crores and the PAT margins of 25%.
We are a debt-free company and main target is to reduce the cost be it to any cost which is incurring to the company.
H2 will definitely be higher than H1 because the bogie production, the new plant production will be from this month.

Complete assembly lines (casting, fabrication, spring and rubber plant), quantum not disclosed

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR210-220 crore (about 62% over FY26 total income of ~INR101 crore) with ~25% PAT margin, backed by the new bogie plant commencing June 2026 (INR77 crore capex, ~INR100 crore expected FY27 contribution) and an INR140-150 crore order book, though the order book figure is loosely stated and no quarterly growth was disclosed.
